info.name: Microsoft Azure AccessControlClient AccessConnector Wayfinding API
Microsoft Azure Use To Calculate The Best Path Between Two Locations Within A Facility

params.name: api-version
params.description: Version number of Azure Maps API.

params.name: routesetId
params.description: The ID of the routeset to query from.

params.name: facilityId
params.description: The identifier of the facility within the routeset where to find the path.

params.name: fromPoint
params.description: The path origin point in the following format: {latitude},{longitude}.

params.name: toPoint
params.description: The path destination in the following format: {latitude},{longitude}.

params.name: avoidFeatures
params.description: To avoid certain types of connectors in the resulting path. Multiple values can be specified.

params.name: minWidth
params.description: The minimum width (in meters) of openings in the searched path. For example, if you specified a minimum width of 0.85, the searched path will avoid openings less than 85 centimeters wide. Note: by using this value, the resulting path points will be buffered from walls and other vertical obstacles by half of the width provided.

items.docs: The Wayfinding Service is part of Creator, and adheres to the [Open Geospatial Consortium](http://docs.opengeospatial.org/is/17-069r3/17-069r3.html) standard. Wayfinding uses indoor map data from the [routeset](/rest/api/maps-creator/routeset) to calculate the best path between two locations within the same facility. For more information, see [Wayfinding](/azure/azure-maps/creator-indoor-maps#wayfinding-preview) in the _Creator for indoor maps_ concepts article.
